stories.headline: Royals send Maikel Garcia to Mariners in six-player trade
stories.summary: The Royals are trading third baseman Maikel Garcia to the Mariners in exchange for right-hander Bryce Miller as part of a six-player trade.
stories.body:
The Kansas City Royals traded third baseman Maikel Garcia to the Seattle Mariners in exchange for right-hander Bryce Miller as part of a six-player trade on Wednesday.

Left-handed reliever Jose Ferrer and right-handed starter Logan Evans are also going to the Royals in the trade, while right-handed reliever James McArthur and minor league reliever LP Langevin are heading to Seattle.

The Royals, desperate to upgrade their starting rotation, had floated Garcia, who turns 27 in March, in trade talks this offseason.

"It is rare to have an opportunity to acquire a player signed for the long term who fits our needs as well as Maikel does," said Jerry Dipoto, the Mariners' president of baseball operations. "His ability to impact the game with his bat, his defense and his baserunning makes us a more athletic and well-rounded team."

Dipoto said recently that one of his primary goals this offseason was to improve the club's defense. Garcia has long been considered a standout glove, and he also offers positional versatility with experience at second base, shortstop and even in the outfield.

The slick-fielding Garcia hit .268 with three home runs and 38 RBIs in just 82 games this season after he had multiple stints on the injured list with a muscle strain in his left hand, which caused him to miss almost two months, and multiple hamstring strains.

He was a first-time All-Star selection and Gold Glove Award winner in 2025, parlaying his success that season into a five-year, $57.5 million deal contract that runs through 2030 and includes a club option for 2031.

"We believe Maikel is one of baseball's best all-around third basemen, and his impact shows up on the field, on the bases and in the batters' box," Mariners executive vice president and general manager Justin Hollander said.

The Mariners were arguably the most disappointing team in baseball this year, finishing 10 games below .500 in a season that began with World Series expectations. Adding a right-handed bat was a priority, especially at third base.

Seattle, with new manager Jason Kanzler, is stocked with starting-pitching depth and the lineup is headlined by two superstars in Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez.

Raleigh, Rodriguez and Josh Naylor, however, struggled mightily this past season, and the Mariners ultimately finished five games behind the Houston Astros in the American League West. Brendan Donovan, acquired in a major offseason trade, was limited to just 39 games. And a rotation headlined by Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo and Miller posted the sixth-highest ERA in the majors after the All-Star break.

Garcia had a breakout season in 2025, hitting .286 with 16 home runs, 81 runs and 74 RBIs while playing in 160 games. He played for Venezuela in the World Baseball Classic prior to this season.

Royals general manager JJ Picollo said after the season that the club would be aggressive in its pursuit of pitching help this offseason, both in the rotation and the bullpen.

Miller, 28, was 4-10 with a 4.17 ERA and 119 strikeouts in 21 starts and one relief appearance. He didn't make his Mariners season debut until May 13 because of a strained left oblique.

The Mariners had declined a $6,075,000 option on Miller, who remains under club control and is eligible for salary arbitration. He got a $15,000 buyout from the Mariners as part of a one-year deal that guaranteed $2,452,500.

He has spent all four of his major league seasons with Seattle, going 28-31 with a 4.04 ERA and 483 strikeouts in 520⅔ innings.

Ferrer, 26, made 73 appearances for Seattle this season, going 4-4 with three saves and a 4.18 ERA in 64⅔ innings pitched. He struck out 54 and walked 20 in his first season with the Mariners after three seasons with the Washington Nationals.

Evans, 25, made 15 starts in his rookie season for Seattle, going 6-5 with a 4.32 ERA and 59 strikeouts in 81⅓ innings.

"I would be remiss if I didn't acknowledge Bryce, Jose and Logan for their contributions to the Mariners," Hollander said. "All three made an impact during their time, and in particular Bryce's contributions from the time he was drafted to today are significant both on the field and in our clubhouse."

McArthur, a right-handed reliever who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in the majors since the 2024 season, when he saved 18 games for the Royals. He missed the 2025 season because of elbow surgery and had hoped to return this past season, but elbow inflammation limited him to four minor league appearances.

ESPN's Alden Gonzalez and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Mammoth, Avalanche bring mountain style to Winter Classic uniforms
stories.summary: A mammoth crest anchors Utah's light blue jersey, while Colorado features a cream jersey with a burgundy "C" surrounding a mountain design.
stories.body:
The NHL Winter Classic in Salt Lake City has inspired a mountain of fashion creativity for the Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche.

The Mammoth will host the Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah on Dec. 31 at 6 p.m. ET. Utah is currently the only NHL team not to have appeared in an outdoor game.

The Winter Classic traditionally features "throwback" uniforms. Utah, in collaboration with the NHL and the league's official uniform maker Fanatics, created a vintage look without having decades of uniforms from which to draw.

"The amazing challenge we had is that it's obviously a two-year-old franchise getting the Winter Classic in its third season. So how do you sort of establish the history and roots of the game in a two-year-old franchise?" Chris Armstrong, Utah's president of hockey operations, told ESPN. "I think we captured that very creatively and very effectively."

Utah has a "mountain blue" jersey with a throwback-inspired rendering of their "walking mammoth" logo. The brown and beige detailing is meant to pay homage to "the fur of a woolly mammoth," according to Fanatics. Inside the hem of the jersey is a hexagon design to honor the state flag as well as "alpine snowflakes" as a nod to vintage ski sweaters.

The Mammoth will wear blue helmets with the word "Utah," and a mammoth tusk crossing the "T."

"It was a very collaborative process between our internal design team, Fanatics and the league," Armstrong said. "We could not be happier with where we landed. Bias aside, I think it's going to be one of the top five, maybe even top three [Winter Classic jerseys]."

Colorado, appearing in its fourth outdoor game, has a Winter Classic jersey that's also alpine-inspired. The front crest features a "Tuscan-style C with mountains nestled inside," according to Fanatics. The lettering on the jersey is meant to evoke the type of signage found in Rocky Mountain towns in the 19th century. On the jersey's hem, a loop tag displays "5280," a nod to Denver's elevation in feet above sea level and its "Mile High City" nickname.

The rest of Colorado's kit has its own Easter eggs. The Winter Classic will mark the first time the Avalanche will wear burgundy helmets, each of them adorned with a Colorado flag. There's also a diamond logo on their burgundy pants, which is a reference to the difficulty rating of ski slopes.

The Winter Classic in Salt Lake City will mark the 47th NHL regular-season outdoor game.

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'
stories.summary: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.
stories.body:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.

Pochettino's final act in charge of the United States national side was a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.

A plane carrying Pochettino arrived at Manchester Airport on Wednesday afternoon. He headed to the club's training ground, Carrington, as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before his first game leading United on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

On Tuesday night, Pochettino was told by former Manchester City and United States player DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue."

He responded: "You will see. Give me time.

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenalin you want to feel. We need to add our common sense... we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing."

Pochettino added: "The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

Upon arrival at Carrington, Pochettino said he is "very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, looking forward to start to work."

United have confirmed Jesus Perez, Miguel D'Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino as Pochettino's staff.

Mauricio Pochettino starts work at Man United on Wednesday

Pochettino was also asked about whether he can improve United's running statistics, which were criticised by ex-boss Carrick after a drab 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

In response to Bruno Fernandes' questioning of the team's tactics, Carrick said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Pochettino said on Tuesday night: "What I can talk in general, football is very complex and I think it's not important if you run or not run.

"You need to run well, you need to run with an objective, you need to run together. Then you need to play, you need to know what you need to do, you need to express your talent. The mindsets are so important."

Pochettino led the U.S. to the round of 16 at last summer's World Cup on home soil.

But he is now returning to the Premier League where he has previously coached Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

The former Argentina international, who also coached Lionel Messi, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé at Paris Saint-Germain between 2021 and 2022, takes over at United with the club in the relegation zone after 10 games.

stories.headline: Kayla Harrison, Amanda Nunes reclaim leading roles in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Who do Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes replace in ESPN's P4P women's top 10?
stories.body:
Hello (again), Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes. Goodbye (for now), Valentina Shevchenko and Zhang Weili. The top of the ESPN women's MMA pound-for-pound rankings has a new look.

Harrison and Nunes, both of whom had been ineligible for the top 10 because of inactivity, returned over the weekend for a clash of elites at UFC 334. Harrison, defending her bantamweight championship for the first time after nearly a year and a half out of the cage while healing from surgery for herniated discs in her neck, scored a fourth-round submission of Nunes, who had been retired for nearly 3½ years. As a result, Harrison takes over the No. 1 ranking and Nunes, a former two-division champion and the consensus GOAT of women's MMA, is No. 2.

The former occupants of those spots, Shevchenko and Zhang, are newly ineligible for the rankings because it's been over a year since they have fought and they have nothing scheduled. Those two former champions drop out, and the rest of the women's top 10 remains the same.

In the men's rankings, UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane moves up one spot to No. 7 on the strength of his decision win over Josh Hokit in their title bout at UFC 334.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Nov. 18. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Kayla Harrison

UFC bantamweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 20-1

Last: W (Sub4) vs. Amanda Nunes, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Harrison stepped into the Octagon at UFC 334 already a reigning champion, but her submission win over Nunes was truly her crowning achievement. The backstory about their shared training gym history added drama to the buildup, but what mattered most about this matchup was that Harrison, who had voiced her goal to be the greatest ever in women's MMA, was facing the woman who has lived up to that standard. After choking out Nunes, what can Harrison do for an encore? Can any other woman in the sport give her a fight? Maybe it won't come to that. Harrison and Nunes both called for a rematch -- but at featherweight. That would lessen Harrison's burden in dealing with her toughest foe: the weigh-in scale.

2. Amanda Nunes

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-6

Last: L (Sub4) vs. Kayla Harrison, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Nunes' return from retirement did not go as she had hoped, but her failing was not so much about deteriorated physical abilities as it was about her ill-advised choice to venture too much into the grappling wheelhouse of Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist. If Nunes gets the rematch both women are calling for, but this time at 145 pounds, that would seem to be to the advantage of Harrison, the bigger woman. But a redo would give Nunes another opportunity to lean into her own prodigious strength as a striker.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 13-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Virna Jandiroba, Nov. 7

Next: TBA

If Suarez was still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Loopy Godínez. Then she went on to beat another fellow top-10 strawweight, Jandiroba, sending a message to the division that Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

8. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

9. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

10. Jasmine Jasudavicius

UFC flyweight

Record: 16-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Erin Blanchfield, Oct. 17

Next: TBA

Jasudavicius was rising in the 125-pound division until being knocked out by Manon Fiorot last year, halting a five-fight winning streak. But she got back up and won two in a row, most recently an impressive grappling performance against Blanchfield, to reassert herself as a contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Kayla Harrison; 2. Amanda Nunes; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Tatiana Suarez; 6. Cris Cyborg; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Manon Fiorot; 9. Dakota Ditcheva; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Nunes; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Jasmine Jasudavicius.

Andrew Davis: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Suarez; 10. Jasudavicius.

Dre Waters: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Nunes; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Joselyne Edwards.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Jasudavicius.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 29-4

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Movsar Evloev, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. He did just that by handing Evloev his first loss at UFC 333.

3. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 21-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career, then completing his trilogy with Dvalishvili with a successful title defense. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet.

4. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

5. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: Jan. 30 vs. Manel Kape

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

7. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 15-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Josh Hokit, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ made his first defense against Hokit at UFC 334, winning a slugfest.

8. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 7

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

9. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 21-6

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. Their third meeting at UFC 333 was the most competitive in their trilogy, but Dvalishvili fell short again.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: Dec. 12 vs. Sergei Pavlovich

Pereira made a big splash in the MMA after a world championship career in kickboxing. He joined the UFC in 2021 and became a middleweight champion the following year, then moved on to be a two-time light heavyweight titlist before making an unprecedented bid for a belt in a third weight class when he fought Game at UFC Freedom 250 for an interim heavyweight title. Pereira got knocked out in that fight, but now he's back on his feet and in position to reclaim his position when he faces a fellow title contender, Pavlovich, at UFC 335.

Other fighters receiving votes: Alexandre Pantoja and Sean Strickland.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Ilia Topuria; 4. Alexander Volkanovski; 5. Joshua Van; 6. Arman Tsarukyan; 7. Merab Dvalishvili; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Gane; 6. Yan; 7. Van; 8. Pereira; 9. Dvalishvili; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Yan; 4. Gaethje; 5. Topuria; 6. Van; 7. Gane; 8. Tsarukyan; 9 Pereira; 10. Sean Strickland.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Yan; 4. Gaethje; 5. Topuria; 6. Van; 7. Dvalishvili; 8. Gane; 9. Pereira; 10. Tsarukyan.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Yan; 3. Volkanovski; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Tsarukyan; 7. Topuria; 8. Gane; 9. Dvalishvili; 10. Alexandre Pantoja.
