Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Paul Goldschmidt, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base
Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop
Some free agents: Ha-Seong Kim, J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners
Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. Karabell (11/18)

Some free agents: Alec Bohm, Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted), Teruaki Sato (posted)

Outfield
Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter
Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/17)

Other free agents: Tarik Skubal, Michael King, Sonny Gray, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers (Q), Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to RHP Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Kaima Taira (posted), Hiromi Itoh (posted)

stories.headline: The NFL's current worst team? Lamar-less Ravens making that case
stories.summary: The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It has been 24 days since they've had a lead.
stories.body:
BALTIMORE -- In the final seconds of Monday night's 23-20 loss to the winless Los Angeles Chargers, Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry voiced his displeasure on the sideline while looking up at the scoreboard.

"This is horrible," Henry said.

In a matter of weeks, the Ravens have gone from being a Super Bowl contender to a team facing a once unthinkable question: Is Baltimore currently the NFL's worst team? The Lamar Jackson-less Ravens have certainly looked like it.

Over the last four weeks, Baltimore has a minus-74 point differential -- 21 points worse than any other NFL team. During this stretch, in which Jackson has been limited to one snap because of ankle and right thumb injuries, the Ravens offense ranks 30th in scoring (13.3 points) and their defense is 28th (31.8).

As far as where the Ravens' frustration ranks, let's just say it's off the charts.

Asked about the level of urgency on the team, Henry snapped back, "How many have we lost in a row? OK, so the urgency should tell you right there. I don't mean to be rude, but you all are asking questions I think you all know the answer to."

The Ravens have gone 38 days without a win. It's been 24 days since they've had a lead.

Baltimore has not led at any point in its past three games. The Ravens haven't had a stretch like this in 19 years.

The message from Ravens coach Jesse Minter to his players: There's no more margin for error.

"Honestly, we have a two-game stretch before our bye to stay alive," Minter said. "That's really where it's at."

After a 4-1 start, Baltimore has seen its season fall apart. The Ravens (4-6) now have a better chance at a top-five pick in the 2027 draft (8.6%) than a playoff spot (4.1%), according to ESPN Analytics.

ESPN's Football Power Index is projecting Baltimore to win one of its final seven games (Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns). After playing on Monday night, the Ravens have a quick turnaround before playing at the Carolina Panthers (4-5) on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) and at the Houston Texans (3-6) the following week.

"It's going to be about getting up off the mat and coming back to work," Minter said. "And I think we have the guys to do that, but we have to do it. We keep talking about things, and [we need] more action."

The Ravens' problems range from self-inflicted mistakes to missed assignments on defense to the inability to run the ball.

BALTIMORE'S ISSUE ON offense has been getting out of its own way. The Ravens have been flagged for a league-worst 55 offensive penalties.

On Monday night, Baltimore hurt itself with a turnover. On a potential comeback drive, wide receiver Zay Flowers had the ball ripped out of his grasp around midfield with two minutes remaining.

Flowers left the locker room as soon as reporters entered, leaving others to explain his critical mistake.

"I mean, he should have held onto the ball," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said. "There are plays that everybody has given up, that I've given up. That's my teammate, and he has made countless plays but he's human, too. The Ravens aren't the Ravens without him, and we believe in him. We love him."

This was Flowers' fourth fumble in the fourth quarter since 2023 (including playoffs), the most among wide receivers during this span. He also made a costly mistake in the 2023 AFC Championship Game, when he fumbled near the goal line in the fourth quarter of a 17-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Flowers did not talk after that game, too.

"He has made plays time and time again, and he's helped this team win a lot of games," tight end Mark Andrews said. "He's a guy who's going to learn from his mistakes and get better from this. I think that at the end of the day, we have to have each other's backs and be on one accord. We talk about that and just [to] stay together, and I for sure have his back."

JESSE MINTER LANDED the Ravens head coach job, in part, because of his defensive expertise. So far, Baltimore is on pace to give up the second-most points in team history.

The Ravens were no match for the top three quarterbacks in the AFC. Joe Burrow put up 35 points on them. Josh Allen totaled 36 points. Trevor Lawrence racked up 33 points.

Then, on Monday night, it wasn't about the quarterback. It was the collapse of the Baltimore run defense.

The common denominator in all those games: There is a disconnect on defense.

"I think the particular reason is everyone wasn't doing their job play in and play out," Ravens middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. "We can all put a hand in it. So, we have to get better. It just comes down to the details. Each and every player has to hone in on their details at the end of the day and be able to come out and play the game the way we want to play."

The Ravens are on pace to allow 440 points, which would fall one point shy of the franchise record (441 in the inaugural season 1996). Trey Hendrickson, the prized free agent addition, has two sacks and seven quarterback hits in eight games. Marlon Humphrey, the team's most experienced cornerback, has allowed the fifth-most passing yards in coverage (425) this season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

Minter believes accountability goes beyond showing up to meetings and practice on time. It's about attention to details.

"Accountability means a lot of different things," Minter said, "but to me, it's really what happens on the field when it matters."

Still, the long-standing identity of this franchise has been to stop the run and establish the run. Can the Ravens do both at a high level?

"I think we have guys that can," Minter said, "but talk is cheap."

THE RAVENS SET a team record on Monday night that they would rather forget. Baltimore managed no yards rushing in the first half.

"Unacceptable," Minter said before adding, "It's embarrassing."

The Ravens offensive line continually got pushed back, and Henry struggled to break tackles. Henry was hit at the line or behind it on eight of 10 carries, which resulted in 10 total rushing yards.

Baltimore finished with 16 yards rushing, which is the third fewest in Ravens history.

"We're just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game," Henry said. "Sixteen total yards is a clear explanation."

What's also clear is how the Ravens perform with and without Jackson, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after having right thumb surgery in early November. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to try to keep the season alive in case Jackson can return, but the playoff chances are quickly dwindling without the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player.

With Jackson as their starting quarterback, the Ravens are 82-38 (.683) and average 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as its starter since 2019, Baltimore is 7-16 (.304) and average 17.4 points per game.

"Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it's a grown-man's league," Henry said. "It hasn't been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. So, of course having [No.] 8 will help, but at the end of the day, we have to go out there and do our jobs."

stories.headline: Boston College to retire late Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 jersey
stories.summary: The Boston College men's hockey team announced Wednesday that it will retire the late Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 on Feb. 12 ahead of its game against the University of Connecticut at Kelley Rink.
stories.body:
The Boston College men's hockey team announced Wednesday that it will retire the late Johnny Gaudreau's No. 13 on Feb. 12 ahead of its game against the University of Connecticut at Kelley Rink.

Gaudreau, who spent three seasons at BC, will become only the third men's player to have his number retired by the school. He joins David Emma and Mike Mottau as the only Eagles to have that distinction.

"We are proud to honor Johnny Gaudreau by retiring his No. 13 at Boston College," BC athletics director Blake James said in a statement. "Johnny was an extraordinary player who helped bring a national championship to the Heights and became one of the most accomplished players in our program's history. He will always hold a special place in the Boston College family."

Gaudreau and his brother Matthew, who played four seasons at BC, were hit and killed in August 2024 while riding their bicycles in Salem County, New Jersey. Sean M. Higgins, who pled not guilty in January 2025, is facing multiple charges including two counts of aggravated manslaughter. Higgins is slated to go to trial in January 2027 after he rejected a plea deal.

Averaging more than a point per game in the United States Hockey League created the belief that Gaudreau could have an impact with the Eagles. In his freshman season, he scored 21 goals and 44 points in 44 games in a campaign that would see Boston College capture the fifth men's national title in program history.

Over the next two years, Gaudreau, who went by the nickname "Johnny Hockey," further established his legacy as one of the most accomplished men's collegiate players of his generation. Gaudreau won the first of consecutive Hockey East Player of the Year awards after scoring 21 goals and 51 points as a sophomore. His junior season saw him score 36 goals and 80 points en route to winning both the Hockey East Player of the Year and the Hobey Baker Award, which goes to the top men's collegiate player.

It was just the third time Boston College had a Hobey Baker winner. The previous recipients were Emma in 1991 and Mottau in 2000.

Gaudreau, who played for both the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets, scored 243 goals and had 743 points in 763 games.

On Tuesday, it was announced that the childhood rink of the Gaudreau brothers would be memorializing them with a bronze statue outside of the facility.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi court reduces sentences for 8 in Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: An Abu Dhabi court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, for their part in last week's wild hotel brawl in the UAE's capital city.
stories.body:
Abu Dhabi's Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants convicted in connection to last week's hotel brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili, according to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department.

The eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, were originally sentenced to six months in prison. Under the revised ruling, which the ADJD released Tuesday, each defendant will instead pay a fine of 150,000 AED (approximately $40,800). The department said the reduced sentence followed a reconciliation between the parties, the mutual withdrawal of claims and appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi government for their release.

The altercation took place Nov. 11 in the lobby of the Yas Hilton Hotel, ahead of RAF's inaugural event in Abu Dhabi. Multiple videos captured Nurmagomedov, who is the PFL lightweight champion and younger cousin of Khabib Nurmagomedov, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face, triggering a brawl between multiple members of both teams. Dvalishvili, who was initially arrested but released, advocated for Nurmagomedov's release Saturday.

Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili have been involved in a long-running feud, dating back to Dvalishvili's UFC title win against Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in January 2025. The camps were involved in a brief altercation at another RAF event in July in Dvalishvili's home country of Georgia. Over the weekend, UFC president Dana White criticized RAF's security measures, saying, "They must like it for this to happen all the time."

RAF founder Chad Bronstein told ESPN the organization regretted the incident, but pushed back on any suggestion it's becoming commonplace.

"Did they have drama in the past? Yeah," Bronstein said of Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili. "But did I think that was going to happen in Abu Dhabi? No. You can always expect there's going to be some words in a press conference ... I didn't think that would happen in a hotel lobby. How many fights have taken place at the UFC, at press conferences, in arenas? We have a great relationship with the UFC, but I think that's an unfair statement."

Bronstein added the incident did not impact RAF's recently-signed deal with the region of Abu Dhabi.

"We're already talking about new events coming up, we have a five-year deal," Bronstein said. "Saturday's event sold out Etihad Arena. I feel like there's going to be a long partnership."

On Monday, RAF announced Dvalishvili and his 21-year-old Georgian teammate Saba Lazishvili have been booked to the promotion's first event in the New York metropolitan area on Dec. 19 at Nassau Coliseum in Long Island.

Dvalishvili will face Kenzo Biyong, a former Dutch professional soccer player from the Netherlands. Lazashvili, who gained a massive online following for his participation in the hotel lobby brawl, will face the winner of a match between Sergio Garcia and Cody Garbrandt at RAF 15 on Nov. 28 in Chicago.

stories.headline: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.

Lando Norris clinched his third victory this season at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in wet conditions.

Max Verstappen had a masterful drive in his Red Bull and charged his way through the field from 21st to second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 21st round.

- Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale

- Wet weather mastery by Norris, Verstappen makes Brazil F1's must-see race

- Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to continue at Racing Bulls for 2027

Las Vegas Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, November 20

Practice One: 00.30 a.m. - 1.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 4 a.m. - 5 a.m.

Saturday, November 21

Final Practice: 00.30 a.m. - 1.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 4 a.m. - 5 a.m.

Sunday, November 22

Las Vegas Grand Prix: 4 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Las Vegas Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit
Las Vegas' race is certainly one of the most newest and flashiest street races with one of the most famous backdrops in the world after it took a spot on the F1 calendar in 2023, costing around $500 million.

The street circuit is one of few night races on the calendar, and includes the city's famous Strip and different landmarks around the city, such as the Bellagio and the Sphere.

The best place to watch the action unfold is from a casino, or West Harmon Zone grandstands. Casinos offer high-end packages to watch in specially built race zones around the circuit, but the grandstands around the final corner and viewing the pit straight still offer a great view.

Las Vegas Grand Prix

Circuit: Las Vegas Strip Circuit; Las Vegas, Nevada

Previous winners in Las Vegas

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: George Russell (Mercedes)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2023

Laps: 50 laps of 4km

Lap record: 1:33.365, Max Verstappen (2023)

Most wins: Verstappen has the most wins with two (2023 and 2025) and George Russell has one.

Most poles: Charles Leclerc (2023), Russell (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Las Vegas Grand Prix is cold with temperatures between 10-14°C.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Norris continued his impressive form in the business end of the season and put in a blistering lap to take pole position.

But come Sunday's race he ran wide at the first corner in an attempt to hold off Red Bull's Verstappen, who took advantage from second to gain the lead.

The Dutchman controlled the lead from that point onwards to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Norris and Oscar Piastri ended up being disqualified from the race for a technical infringement -- a major blow in the title race with only two races to go at the time.

Who will win this year?

Mercedes completed the double and wrapped up the constructors' championship last time out, a week after Antonelli was crowned world champion.

With it being a night race, the conditions in Las Vegas are always very cold, a world away from some of the soaring temperatures the drivers race in throughout the year.

McLaren has been running a heavily-upgraded car that seems to be working well, and Norris will be carrying his winning momentum to Vegas.

Verstappen is in strong form and has made his way to second in the title standings with three victories under his belt and 12 podiums this year.

Having won twice in Vegas already, the Dutchman will certainly be the one to watch.

stories.headline: Nike replaces Adidas as UEFA ball provider to restyle Champions League
stories.summary: The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.
stories.body:
The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.

A match ball manufactured by Adidas, with the famous star-studded ball used for Europe's premier competition, will be used for the final time in the 2026-27 final.

There has been no confirmation as to whether the new Nike ball will retain the star pattern used in the competitions logo. UEFA said in a statement: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course.."

- Why the Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced

From 2027-28, U.S. brand Nike will take over as the official ball supplier for UEFA for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

German brand Adidas had been the ball supplier for the UEFA Champions League since 2001 but their long-standing association with the competition is now coming to an end.

Nike went into exclusive talks in April with the agency that handles all commercial deals for UEFA club competitions, a subsidiary of United States-based Relevent.

Relevent was appointed last year by the commercial joint venture between UEFA and the increasingly influential European Football Clubs group, which has seen long-standing sponsor deals end.

Relevent was co-founded by Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross and also has a long-term deal with UEFA to market commercial rights for national team competitions.

Total broadcast and sponsor revenue for UEFA men's club competitions is projected to rise above 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) starting next season.

Camilo Andrade, Vice President and General Manager of Nike Football, said: "We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football's biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA's men's club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time.

"Football is the world's game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common. This is a long-term commitment for Nike. We will listen to the athlete's voice, push the edges of innovation, honour the prestige and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans."

Guy-Laurent Epstein, Co-Managing Director UC3 -- which unites UEFA to Europe's clubs -- said: "We are delighted to welcome Nike as the official match ball provider for UEFA men's club competitions from 2027. Nike brings an incredible combination of sporting heritage, creativity and cultural influence, with an ability to connect with fans around the world. We look forward to working together, both on and off the pitch, to deliver innovation, quality and performance at every level of European club football."

Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: MLS wild card predictions: Who will emerge from Orlando-Cincinnati, Seattle-RSL?
stories.summary: The wild card kicks off the MLS Cup playoffs on Thursday, so who will advance to Round 1? ESPN's U.S. soccer analysts make their predictions.
stories.body:
The international break may not be quite over just yet, but in MLS, attention is already returning to the club game. That's because the opening salvos of the MLS Cup playoffs begin on Thursday with the wild-card round.

Having 18 of the league's 30 teams qualify for the postseason might make for a bloated playoff field, but who doesn't love a play-in game? Thursday night will see the eighth and ninth seeds of both conferences square off for a date with the No. 1-ranked side in the East and West.

So, Orlando City vs. FC Cincinnati, Seattle Sounders vs. Real Salt Lake, how will it all play out? Who will advance? Joseph Lowery breaks down the matchups and ESPN's U.S. soccer analysts make their predictions.

Eastern Conference
8. Orlando City vs. 9. FC Cincinnati
Star attraction: There's exactly one outfield player in MLS who's been more transformational than Antoine Griezmann -- and it's Lionel Messi. Among current players with at least 1,000 minutes this year, the FIFA World Cup winner with France is the closest to Messi when it comes to goal contributions per game. Posting a staggering 1.06 combined goals and assists per 90 minutes, Orlando City's star summer signing completely changed their fortunes.

Before Griezmann, Orlando found itself near the East's basement with 14 points in 15 games and a defense hemorrhaging goals. With the former Atlético Madrid attacker in tow, the club's points per game shot up from 0.93 to 1.68, good for the sixth-best tally in MLS since the World Cup break. The Lions are still leaking goals, though -- their 78 conceded this season is tied for the second-most in league history -- but with Griezmann's passing range and goal threat, they truly can outscore their opponents and make some noise.

X-factor: It takes a serious player to nab top billing from Evander, Cincinnati's superstar No. 10, but that's exactly what Griezmann's presence in Orlando has done. Still, both teams will take pains to limit the other's elite creator. While keeping their opponent's star quiet will be a nearly impossible feat for the second- and third-worst defensive teams in MLS, that Orlando City will be paying special attention to Evander will open space for Pavel Bucha.

Outside of Evander and the team's center-back corps, no Cincinnati regular touches the ball more than Bucha. According to American Soccer Analysis, the Czechia international central midfielder takes 8.1% of his team's touches. Bucha's service even prompted manager Pat Noonan to play him as a right wingback earlier this year. Back in the center, the 28-year-old will have a chance to provide the creative touch for the visitors.

Tactical wrinkle: It's all well and good for Cincinnati to have Griezmann at the top of the scouting report and for Orlando to do the same with Evander. Slowing those players down is another matter entirely. How effectively each team accomplishes that task could decide Thursday's match.

Orlando had exactly one true center back in its squad on Decision Day. The Lions have been hurting for quality central defenders, and that pain only increased when Robin Jansson went down with a season-ending injury. Just how will interim manager Martín Perelman compensate for being perilously thin in the back?

Cincinnati, for its part, spent more on salaries for defenders than any other team this year as of the MLS Players Association's May release. Try as Noonan might, defensive stability has evaded his team. They'll need to find another level without the ball to keep Orlando's high-powered attack quiet.

Predictions
Orlando has the luxury of playing at home and will have the best player on the field in Griezmann. Between the Frenchman, Martín Ojeda, Marco Pasalic, and U.S. men's national teamer Justin Ellis, Orlando City's attacking arsenal will be too much for Cincinnati to handle. -- Lowery

Neither of these teams is very good defensively, but Cincinnati seemed to get its act together toward the end of the season. Evander vs. Griezmann should be fun, but I expect Cincinnati to come out on top. -- Jeff Carlisle

You can't overlook the form of Griezmann. He's got nine goal contributions in his past seven games for Orlando and will likely be the difference-maker in this matchup. -- Cesar Hernandez

This match feels more like a Round 1 matchup with MVP finalist Evander taking on Newcomer of the Year finalist Griezmann. Despite two good sides, Orlando should be able to capitalize on the Frenchman's magic to advance. -- Lizzy Becherano

Western Conference
8. Seattle Sounders vs. 9. Real Salt Lake
Star attraction: There was no bigger breakout star in MLS this year than Real Salt Lake striker Sergi Solans. The Spaniard has taken an atypical path, beginning in the Girona academy before heading to Oregon State, being drafted by Salt Lake, going back to school, transferring to UCLA, and now shining in MLS. Solans finished tied for eighth in non-penalty goals (15) during his rookie campaign. So impressive was the 23-year-old that RSL handed him a new contract months into the campaign.

Even with Zavier Gozo's August departure and Diego Luna 's season-ending injury, Solans managed six goals in his final eight games of the regular season. The No. 9 is a workhorse atop head coach Pablo Mastroeni's 3-4-3 attacking setup and it's hard to picture him lasting long in MLS before a European club comes knocking.

X-factor: The Sounders were getting desperate. They'd lost eight games in a row from the middle of May to the middle of August, a streak that seemed unthinkable for a team with Seattle's level of depth and experience. But with a growing injury list and a lengthy barren run, the team needed change. Enter: star striker Dejan Joveljic. In their first notable acquisition involving a transfer fee since Pedro de la Vega joined in 2024, the Sounders spent $6 million in a cash-for-player trade to snag Joveljic from Sporting Kansas City.

Immediately thrust into manager Brian Schmetzer's starting lineup, the Serbia international bagged a brace in his Seattle debut and collected four goals in his first five games. Since then? He's scored just one in six matches. Reliant on service, Joveljic doesn't have the benefit of being surrounded by a consistent or balanced attack. There's a reason his goals have come in bunches, after all.

If the Sounders manage to feed Joveljic on Thursday, they'll put themselves in the driver's seat. If not, the striker's barren run will likely continue as his team's playoff run ends.

Tactical wrinkle: In an underrated pickup, Real Salt Lake signed Canada's starting center back at the World Cup Luc de Fougerolles on loan from Fulham in the summer. The 21-year-old has been tasked with a fascinating role by Mastroeni -- one not dissimilar to how Wilfried Nancy used Steven Moreira during the Columbus Crew 's MLS Cup run in 2023. Constantly encouraged to push into the attack from his right-sided center-back spot, De Fougerolles leads all central defenders with at least 500 minutes this year in passes and touch share in the final third, as per ASA. The next closest true center back to De Fougerolles? Moreira himself.

With the Canadian eager to help RSL overload the attack, Seattle will have its hands full maintaining numerical parity in the back. But if the Sounders can stymie Salt Lake's aggressive possession positioning, they'll have chances to attack the visitors on the break.

Predictions
In the three years of MLS' current playoff format, the lower-seeded wild-card team has won just once in six tries. The odds, then, are in Seattle's favor despite Salt Lake's stronger form heading into this meeting. -- Lowery

The rosters of both teams have been in flux this season, Seattle due to injuries and RSL due to the same plus the transfer of Gozo. But of the two teams, Seattle has the experience to progress, especially in midfield with Hassani Dotson and Cristian Roldan. -- Carlisle

It's going to be a tough one for Brian Schmetzer & Co., but they have enough playoff experience to get this over the line. Keep an eye on Albert Rusnák, who has a goal and two assists in his past two appearances. -- Hernandez

The Sounders went through a difficult season, but Schmetzer's experience in the league can work to out-coach Salt Lake to earn the victory. -- Becherano

stories.headline: 2027 WNBA mock draft: Tempo win lottery, projected to pick JuJu Watkins at No. 1
stories.summary: Toronto edged Houston and got the top pick in Sunday's draft lottery. The Comets will pick No. 2 and the Mystics No. 3.
stories.body:
In what could be the JuJu Watkins sweepstakes, the Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft. The Tempo won the draft lottery Sunday, with the Houston Comets picking second and the Washington Mystics third.

The Seattle Storm have the No. 4 pick, the Portland Fire got No. 5 and the Los Angeles Sparks have Nos. 6 and 7.

The Tempo, an expansion team in 2026, finished 11-33 last season, missing the playoffs. They were last in the league in defensive rating and won just one game after the All-Star break.

All of that could be much improved in 2027 with a player such as Watkins in Toronto. The national player of the year as a sophomore for the USC Trojans, Watkins missed last season after a knee injury suffered in the 2025 NCAA tournament. She has looked great so far this season and would fit in well with any WNBA team.

This is just Watkins' third college season, but age-wise, she is eligible for the draft. It is unknown if she will go pro or return to USC, but for now we are including her in the mock draft. If she decides Toronto is an unappealing destination or just wants to spend another season in college, she can wait until the 2028 draft.

That said, there is also uncertainty about the seniors who already have completed three seasons. Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model -- the five-seasons-in-five-years rule -- they could return for the 2027-28 season. So a lot about the draft pool remains speculative.

But now we know the lottery order.

1. Toronto Tempo: JuJu Watkins
USC | guard | 6-foot-2 | senior

Watkins and the Trojans are 3-1 after a close loss Sunday to No. 1 South Carolina in which she had 25 points. The March 2025 knee injury that forced Watkins to miss last season has not slowed her. She is averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals. The Tempo's strength last season was at guard, led by Marina Mabrey. If Watkins doesn't declare for the draft, there should still be good players available for the Tempo. But perhaps not an immediate franchise-changer as Watkins is expected to be.

2. Houston Comets: Madison Booker
Texas | forward | 6-foot-1 | senior

Like several teams, Texas has not been tested yet. But Booker has displayed why she's a lottery pick in the three games she has played so far, including a 30-point, six-assist game against Northern Colorado. Booker's size, strength and confidence on offense and her versatility on defense should translate to the pro game. She took a hard fall in Wednesday's win over South Dakota State and did not play in Sunday's victory against Tarleton State, but she is not expected to miss much more time. The Comets -- the Connecticut Sun relocated as a revived franchise -- last played in the 2008 WNBA season. The Sun were tied for next to last with Toronto at 11-33 this year, and it's fair to say they could use help in all areas, which would make Booker appealing.

3. Washington Mystics: Hannah Hidalgo
Notre Dame | guard | 5-foot-6 | senior

Hidalgo has carried a heavy load throughout her college career, and that continues her senior season. In four victories, she has averaged 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals while shooting 59.4% from the field. Hidalgo is a huge threat on offense and defense and could really add to the young core already there if she goes to the Mystics. Washington could use more 3-point shooting. While Hidalgo wasn't great from beyond the arc last season (36 of 142, 25.4%), she shot 40% from 3-point range as a sophomore and is at 40% so far this season.

4. Seattle Storm: Tessa Johnson
South Carolina | guard | 6-foot-1 | senior

Johnson's 3-point shooting is an impressive tool that will translate to the pro game. She was the top power-conference player in the country last season in 3-point percentage (44.8%, 90 of 201). So far this season, she is 9-for-18 (50%) from beyond the arc and is averaging 17.0 points. She had 28 points in Sunday's victory over USC. The Storm were last in the WNBA this past season at 8-36 and could benefit from another dynamic young guard to go along with the young post talent they have.

5. Portland Fire: Mikaylah Williams
LSU | guard | 6-foot | senior

The Tigers have cruised through four blowouts, and Williams' averages -- 19.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists while shooting 58% from the field and 45.5% from beyond the arc -- don't tell us anything we didn't expect. She's a pro-ready player on the offensive end who can look to improve defensively in the WNBA. The expansion Fire had a solid season in 2025, going 17-27, and Williams could fit in offensively.

6. Los Angeles Sparks: Kymora Johnson
Virginia | guard | 5-foot-7 | senior

The Cavaliers are 5-0, and we will know more about them once they play their tougher nonconference foes, such as Oklahoma on Nov. 23. But so far, Johnson has looked very good, averaging 18.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 2.2 steals while shooting 59.6% from the field and 61.3% from beyond the arc (13 of 21). With back-to-back picks, Los Angeles can address two of several needs with this draft. The Sparks were 16-28 this season and missed the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.

7. Los Angeles Sparks: Sarah Cissé
France | forward | 6-foot-2

There's so much we don't know now about the Sparks -- including who their coach will be for 2027 -- as they move on after future Hall of Famer Nneka Ogwumike's retirement. But Cissé is another talented player out of France who could make an impact on the WNBA. The MVP of the U20 European Championships this summer, she turns 20 in January. The Sparks were next to last in the WNBA in rebounding this past season, so Cissé might be able to help there.

8. New York Liberty: Ainhoa Risacher
France | forward | 6-foot-1

If you recognize the last name, Risacher is the younger sister of Zaccharie Risacher, the NBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2024. A good-sized wing player, Risacher competed alongside Cissé on France's winning U20 European Championships team this past summer. She will turn 20 in July. The Liberty had an up-and-down 2026 season, getting the No. 8 seed in the playoffs. They knocked off No. 1 Minnesota but then were swept by No. 4 Atlanta. New York fired Chris DeMarco after just one season, so we await their next coach. The Liberty already have a strong French/international presence. The question might be if Risacher impresses them enough defensively compared with other draft options.

9. Dallas Wings: Chloe Kitts
South Carolina | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Kitts missed last season because of a knee injury but has looked great so far. A starter as a junior, she averaged 10.2 points and 7.7 rebounds in 2024-25. Through four games this season, she has three double-doubles and is averaging 13.0 points and 10.0 rebounds. In Sunday's victory over USC, Kitts had 15 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. If she continues to play this well, we could see her move up the draft board. Still, with Dallas having young guards such as Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd, Kitts could be a good addition for the Wings, who made the playoffs at 27-17 this season.

10. Indiana Fever: Talaysia Cooper
Ole Miss | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

The Fever are facing two huge offseason questions: Will free agent guard Kelsey Mitchell return, and who will be their general manager? Indiana could use help at the wing position with a player who can defend at a high level but also score. That could be Cooper, who is playing for her third SEC program and averaging 14.0 points while shooting 37% (10 of 27) from 3-point range. She showed progress from beyond the arc last season, and if that continues this season it will help her draft prospects. Cooper had her best defensive season as a sophomore at Tennessee, and a return to that level will boost her.

11. Chicago Sky: Khamil Pierre
NC State | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Pierre doesn't shoot the 3 much, but she is relentless in the paint. After two strong years at Vanderbilt, she transferred to NC State and led the ACC in rebounding last season (11.9 RPG) while averaging 16.7 points and shooting 52.5% from the field. So far this season for the 4-1 Wolfpack, she is averaging 21.2 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting 51.3%. The injury-plagued Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs for the third year in a row this past season. They were 13th in offensive rating and 10th in rebounding, and Pierre might help in both areas.

12. Chicago Sky: S'Mya Nichols
Kansas | guard | 6-foot | senior

Nichols is off to a little slower start than expected, averaging 12.5 points and 4.3 assists. (She averaged 17.4 and 4.6 last season.) That's why she has fallen from No. 6 in our two previous mock drafts. But to be fair, it's still early in the season. Nichols had 12 points and six assists in the Jayhawks' loss to Nebraska on Saturday. She and Kansas have another shot at a ranked team this week at Minnesota on Wednesday.

13. Dallas Wings: Kaylene Smikle
Tennessee | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

Smikle started her career at Rutgers, then went to Maryland and is now at Tennessee. She played just seven games last year with the Terps, missing the rest of the season after knee surgery. So far this season, she is leading the 4-0 Lady Vols with 22.3 points per game, while also averaging 6.0 rebounds. She is also off to a hot start from beyond the arc at 50% (12 of 24). Smikle could add guard/wing depth for Dallas.

14. Golden State Valkyries: Oluchi Okananwa
Maryland | guard | 5-foot-10 | senior

Okananwa is averaging 14.0 points and 6.3 rebounds, but the Terps have played just three games. She was first-team All-Big Ten and all-defense last season -- we know the WNBA champion Valkyries love defense -- but she probably will need to show improvement as a 3-point shooter to ensure being a first-round pick. So far this season she is 3-for-6 from beyond the arc.

15. Minnesota Lynx: Clara Strack
Kentucky | center | 6-foot-5 | senior

Sunday was another big stats day for Strack, who had 29 points and 18 rebounds in a victory over Eastern Michigan. That included going 4-of-5 from beyond the arc, which is important: It's not easy for traditional centers to find their way in the WNBA, so having shooting range matters. Strack has shown that, making 42 3-pointers over the past two seasons. She is 8-of-21 from 3-point range so far this season. Strack, who was the SEC's defensive player of the year in 2025, is averaging 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds and 3.8 blocks for the 5-0 Wildcats.

stories.headline: First-half romp powers Jillaroos' fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup salute
stories.summary: Australia's Jillaroos have blown away New Zealand 34-10 to win a fourth-straight Women's Rugby League World Cup.
stories.body:
Australia have underlined their women's rugby league dominance with a 34-10 annihilation of New Zealand in the World Cup final.

The Jillaroos did the damage with six first-half tries on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, with winger Jaime Chapman recording a brilliant hat-trick before the break to cap a historic tournament.

It was Australia's fourth straight Cup triumph, following a 54-4 win in the final four years ago and coming after New Zealand won the first three tournaments between 2000-08.

Chapman carried two players more than 10 metres to score her first, before flying into the corner for another and then busting through four tacklers for a sensational 70-metre solo effort.

Her treble gave her the equal record for tries in a World Cup -- for men or women -- at 13, matching the Kiwi Ferns' Honey Hireme-Smiler from 2017.

It seemed inevitable that she would go clear in the second half.

But both teams struggled in the Brisbane humidity, with the Kiwi Ferns' try in the finals seconds the only points of an error-riddled second period.

For the Jillaroos there were several poignant narratives to come out of the win.

Coach Jess Skinner's controversial decision to play five-eighth Jesse Southwell and drop Jocelyn Kelleher paid dividends.

Southwell schemed with the ball, landed five goals and was the perfect foil for half Tarryn Aiken, who controlled play with confidence and skill.

Chapman played in the pool games and semi-final in the 2022 World Cup but has now put an indelible stamp on a final.

"There is no better win than winning the World Cup on home turf," she told Channel Seven.

"We connected the first day we came into camp."

Fullback Tamika Upton sat out the tournament four years ago with a calf injury but now the five-time premiership winner has every team accolade in the game to her credit.

Prop Millie Elliott retires with a fairytale ending while dual international Sariah Paki, who was chased by the Ferns to play for them, has now won the World Cup in two sports after triumphing with the Australian rugby sevens side in 2022.

All the talk before the clash was the danger posed by New Zealand's Golden Boot winner and strike centre Stacey Waaka.

The former rugby union star, who had scored nine tries in the tournament, was snuffed out by Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly, who confronted Waaka all match and gave her no space.

As the Jillaroos' big guns stood up, centre Jessica Sergis scored her 23rd try in 18 Tests with a 70m dash through the middle off an undetected forward pass.

Aiken turned second-rower Shaylee Bent inside for the second try of the match while Upton started and finished a movement that had her attacking fingerprints all over it.

Ferns fullback Apii Nicholls was her side's best player in a dynamic display until she tore a hamstring in the 66th minute.
